provenance.operationalisation_source: Effenberger and Pelanek detector design where explicitly selected by the researcher

global_rules.priority: precision and reproducibility over exhaustive detection
global_rules.prevalence_unit: one valid submission for one programming task
global_rules.safe_default: Do not report a defect unless the structural or source evidence satisfies the documented rule.

boolean_proof.rule: Treat an expression as Boolean only when syntax or simple local data flow establishes a Boolean result.
local_data_flow_sources: parameter or name with an explicit Boolean task contract

allowed_by_role.n: numeric size, count, or bound when that role is clear
allowed_by_role.m: numeric size, count, or bound when that role is clear
allowed_by_role.x: mathematical or coordinate variable, or explicitly specified task name
allowed_by_role.y: mathematical or coordinate variable, or explicitly specified task name
allowed_by_role.z: mathematical or coordinate variable, or explicitly specified task name

duplicate_expression.normalisation: AST structural normalisation preserving expression meaning
duplicate_expression.potentially_side_effecting_calls: All calls not explicitly allowlisted, including input, print, random, file operations, mutating methods, and unknown user-defined functions.

while_as_for.published_structural_rule: The loop test contains exactly one variable updated by a constant each iteration; other condition variables remain unchanged in the body.
while_as_for.additional_safety_rule: The counter update must occur on every executable path through the body.
excluded_constructs: continue that can bypass the update

magic_number.conditional_exemption: -1 is exempt only in a clearly conventional sentinel or index role.
magic_number.literal_2: Not globally exempt; classify from context.
magic_number.task_specification_values: Not exempt solely because they originate in the task specification.

included_rules: missing or inconsistent spaces around assignment, comparison, and Boolean operators
unnecessary spaces immediately inside parentheses, brackets, or braces
whitespace before commas, semicolons, or ordinary colons
whitespace between a function name and its opening parenthesis
whitespace between a collection and its indexing bracket
non-standard four-space indentation where stylistic indentation is applicable
excluded_rules: subjective operator spacing in complex mathematical formulas

defects.name: redundant_if_else
defects.authoritative_definition: An if-else statement directly returns opposite Boolean constants even though the condition itself could be returned.
defects.positive_condition: An If has an else branch and both branches directly return opposite Boolean constants corresponding to the condition.
false_positive_risks: nested control flow mistaken for direct returns

defects.name: redundant_comparison
defects.authoritative_definition: A Boolean expression is explicitly compared with True or False when the expression itself or its direct negation is sufficient.
defects.positive_condition: A == or != comparison has a Boolean constant operand and the other operand is statically established to produce Boolean.
exclusions: comparisons not using True or False

defects.name: redundant_not
defects.authoritative_definition: A comparison is negated with not even though an equivalent direct comparison operator would express the same condition more clearly.
defects.positive_condition: not is applied directly to a single comparison whose operator has a known inverse comparison operator.
exclusions: membership and identity comparisons without a documented safe inverse
false_positive_risks: incorrect inversion of membership or identity operators

defects.name: duplicate_if
defects.authoritative_definition: Consecutive conditional branches contain identical bodies and could be combined by joining their conditions.
defects.positive_condition: Adjacent if/elif branches have structurally equivalent bodies and combining their conditions preserves branch coverage and order.
false_positive_risks: AST equality hiding differing evaluation context

defects.name: else_if
defects.authoritative_definition: An else branch contains only another if statement where elif would express the same conditional chain more directly.
defects.positive_condition: An else branch consists solely of another If, with no meaningful wrapper statements, and the nested form preserves evaluation order.
exclusions: nested If with altered scope or effects
false_positive_risks: comments and source layout not represented by AST
else blocks whose nesting is intentional

defects.name: nested_if
defects.authoritative_definition: A conditional is unnecessarily nested inside another conditional when conditions can be joined using and without changing behavior.
ast_structures: If whose relevant body contains one nested If
defects.positive_condition: The nested condition can be joined with the outer condition and the relevant body has no behavior that would be changed by flattening.

defects.name: redundant_elif
defects.authoritative_definition: An elif is already guaranteed by earlier conditions and could be else.
defects.positive_condition: The preceding branch conditions prove that an elif condition is necessarily true whenever control reaches it.

defects.name: empty_if
defects.authoritative_definition: A conditional branch contains only pass and can be simplified by inverting or restructuring the condition.
defects.positive_condition: An if or else branch contains only pass and the alternative branch contains the meaningful behavior.
exclusions: pass used as deliberate placeholder outside the task behavior
false_positive_risks: branch required by an external contract

defects.name: redundant_indexing
defects.authoritative_definition: A for loop iterates through sequence indices and uses the loop index only to read the current element.
defects.positive_condition: Every meaningful use of the loop index is the matching sequence[index] read; no indexed assignment or meaningful index use occurs.
exclusions: multiple collections indexed by the same variable

defects.name: misleading_iterator_name
defects.authoritative_definition: A loop variable uses an index-style name even though it directly represents collection elements.
defects.positive_condition: A configured index-style name such as i or j is the direct iterator target of a non-index collection.
exclusions: task-scaffolded names when the role is explicit
false_positive_risks: short names accepted by local course convention
iterables whose semantic role is unknown

defects.name: duplicate_expression
defects.authoritative_definition: The same non-trivial expression is repeated where storing its value would avoid unnecessary duplication.
defects.positive_condition: A pure, structurally equivalent expression occurs at least twice in a sufficiently small region and has weighted complexity at least 8.
false_positive_risks: normalised expressions with different runtime behavior

defects.name: while_as_for
defects.authoritative_definition: A while loop is used when the number or range of iterations is known before the loop begins and a for loop would express it more directly.
defects.positive_condition: The test has exactly one control variable updated by a constant on every executable path, other test variables are unchanged, and the loop has no break, return, or bypassing continue.

defects.name: redundant_for
defects.authoritative_definition: A for loop performs zero or a single iteration, making the loop unnecessary.
defects.positive_condition: The iterable is statically determinable to contain zero or one element and the loop action is not repetition-dependent.
exclusions: loops where control flow changes meaning

defects.name: augmentable_assignment
defects.authoritative_definition: A variable update is written as a normal assignment where an augmented assignment would express the same update more directly.
defects.positive_condition: An assignment target is structurally equivalent to one operand of a compatible binary operation on the right-hand side, with numeric behavior preserved.
exclusions: subscript or attribute aliasing without proof
operations without a compatible augmented form

defects.name: inappropriate_formatting
defects.authoritative_definition: Valid Python violates the fixed subset of generally accepted whitespace and formatting conventions.
defects.positive_condition: At least one included formatting rule is violated while tokenization and parsing remain valid.
false_positive_risks: formatting accepted by the local style guide

defects.name: magic_number
defects.authoritative_definition: An unnamed numeric literal with domain or decision-making meaning is embedded directly in logic.
defects.positive_condition: A numeric literal occurs in decision or domain computation logic, is not an approved structural value, and has meaningful semantic role.
exclusions: literals outside decision or computation logic

defects.name: one_letter_name
defects.authoritative_definition: A variable uses a one-letter name where a more descriptive name would improve readability, excluding conventional short names appropriate to context.
defects.positive_condition: A local or parameter one-letter identifier is not task-imposed and is not allowed by the documented role-sensitive policy.
false_positive_risks: course scaffolding not represented in source

defects.name: built_in_name
defects.authoritative_definition: A user-defined variable shadows a Python built-in function or type.
defects.positive_condition: A user-defined identifier is in the configured Python built-in name set and is used as a binding.
exclusions: names explicitly required by task scaffolding unless researcher chooses otherwise
false_positive_risks: built-in set varying across Python versions
